title: Can you draw a feedback loop?
hook: Update two variables simultaneously, then draw their arrows across time.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: a feedback cycle becomes an ordinary graph once drawn across time steps.

misconception: Treating unroll the loop as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: a feedback cycle becomes an ordinary graph once drawn across time steps.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: Start A₀=B₀=0 with Aₜ₊₁=.5Bₜ and Bₜ₊₁=Aₜ+1. After two simultaneous updates, what state appears?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-unroll-the-loop/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Two-period feedback A(t+1)=.5B(t),B(t+1)=A(t)+1; startA0=B0=0. States t1(0,1),t2(.5,1),t3(.5,1.5),t4(.75,1.5). Unroll arrows into time layers, no within-time DAGcycle.

claims.text: Two updates retain A=0.5, B=1; four retain A=0.75, B=1.5. Each update uses the previous time’s values simultaneously.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-unroll-the-loop/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Two-period feedback A(t+1)=.5B(t),B(t+1)=A(t)+1; startA0=B0=0. States t1(0,1),t2(.5,1),t3(.5,1.5),t4(.75,1.5). Unroll arrows into time layers, no within-time DAGcycle.

claims.text: The feedback exists across time, not as a same-instant directed cycle. Unrolling time makes each arrow point from a prior state to a later state, giving an acyclic representation of this dynamic system.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-unroll-the-loop/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Two-period feedback A(t+1)=.5B(t),B(t+1)=A(t)+1; startA0=B0=0. States t1(0,1),t2(.5,1),t3(.5,1.5),t4(.75,1.5). Unroll arrows into time layers, no within-time DAGcycle.
